plan.title: bug(review-cycle): documented lifecycle:event approval recorder is absent from consumer surface

narratives.Description: Review-cycle documents a lifecycle:event approval recorder that is absent from the consumer Taskfile/CLI surface. Real merge-gate approval after operator consent fails when the mandatory command is missing.
narratives.Overview:
## Summary

The shipped `deft-directive-review-cycle` skill mandates a structural approval event through `task lifecycle:event`, but the 0.79.0 npm consumer deposit exposes neither that Task target nor a corresponding CLI verb. An agent following the mandatory Phase 5 to Phase 6 gate cannot record `plan:approved` as instructed.

## Environment

- `@deftai/directive` / `@deftai/directive-core` 0.79.0
- canonical npm consumer deposit under `.deft/core/`
- macOS, Node 24.18.0, Task 3.50.0

## Shipped contract

`.deft/core/skills/deft-directive-review-cycle/SKILL.md` says:

```text
When the user replies yes / confirmed / approve on a ready-to-merge PR thread,
emit a plan:approved framework event via task lifecycle:event so the approval is
captured as a structural artifact rather than prose-only.
```

It then prescribes:

```text
task lifecycle:event -- emit plan:approved ...
```

This is a mandatory review-cycle step, not optional guidance.

## Reproduction

```text
$ task --list-all | rg 'lifecycle:event'
# no result

$ task lifecycle:event -- --help
task: Task "lifecycle:event" does not exist
```

The global 0.79.0 CLI dispatch registry likewise has no `lifecycle:event` verb.

## Expected

One authoritative, npm-consumer-safe surface must exist and match the skill exactly. Either:

1. ship `task lifecycle:event` plus the corresponding Directive CLI handler for `emit plan:approved`; or
2. update the skill to name an existing structural event recorder that is present in the consumer deposit.

The command should be idempotent for a repeated approval of the same PR and HEAD SHA, write to the documented structural artifact, and fail before any merge when its payload is invalid.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A clean 0.79+ consumer install can execute the approval-recording command named by the review-cycle skill.
- [ ] `task --list-all` exposes the documented target and `directive --help` exposes the corresponding verb.
- [ ] The command records `plan:approved` with repository, PR, approved HEAD SHA, actor, and timestamp.
- [ ] Repeating the same event is idempotent or deterministically deduplicated.
- [ ] Review-cycle contract tests fail if the mandatory command disappears from the deposited Taskfile/CLI surface.
- [ ] The skill, commands reference, task description, and CLI help use the same spelling and argument shape.

## Related

- #1670 owns the unified Directive verb vocabulary.
- The defect surfaced during a real consumer PR merge gate after the operator explicitly approved the merge.
narratives.UserStory: As a consumer agent running review-cycle, I want the documented lifecycle:event approval recorder available on the deposited Taskfile/CLI surface, so that merge-gate approval recording does not fail as a missing command.
narratives.ImplementationPlan:
1. Locate the documented lifecycle:event approval recorder in review-cycle skill/docs and reconcile with the deposited Taskfile/CLI.
2. Expose or rename the command so skill, commands.md, task description, and CLI help share one spelling/argument shape.
3. Add a contract test that fails if the mandatory command disappears from the deposited surface.
4. CHANGELOG [Unreleased].

narrative.Acceptance: Given a consumer .deft/core deposit, when the documented approval recorder is invoked, then the command exists on Taskfile/CLI.
Given skill, commands reference, task description, and CLI help, when compared, then they use the same spelling and argument shape.
Given the deposited surface, when contract tests run, then they fail if the mandatory command disappears.
